newsitem.title: USA: Fla. firm indicted on alleged illegal freon import.
newsitem.headline: Fla. firm indicted on alleged illegal freon import.

text.p: A Miami company and three residents were indicted for allegedly illegally importing ozone-depleting refrigerant gases and failing to pay more than $22 million in excise taxes, the Justice Department said on Thursday.

In the largest environmental excise tax case ever, the 164-count indictment unsealed in Miami charged Refrigeration U.S.A. Inc. and Miami residents Roland Wood, Diane McNally and Lisa Salazar with importing more than 4,000 tonnes of freon, more than they were legally allowed to import. It said they then sold the refrigerant without paying all the excise taxes.

Freon is heavily regulated by U.S. laws and an international agreement to reduce the use of such chemicals that deplete the atmosphere's ozone layer. U.S. use of freon was largely phased out as of January unless importers had unused allowances to cover amounts they wanted to import.
"Miami continues to be a hub for a thriving black market in these chemicals," U.S. Attorney William Keefer said in a statement.
Federal authorities have a task force led by the Justice Department to stop smuggling of the refrigerants.
